teach.text: Say **مَرْحَبًا** (marhaban) for “hello.” You can also greet someone with **السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ** (as-salaamu 'alaykum), meaning “peace be upon you.” The reply is **وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ** (wa 'alaykumu s-salaam), “and upon you peace.”
Say **صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ** (sabaaHu l-khayr) for “good morning” and **مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ** (masaa'u l-khayr) for “good evening.”
Use **مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ** (ma'a s-salaama) to say “goodbye.” Say **شُكْرًا** (shukran) for “thank you” and **عَفْوًا** ('afwan) for “you're welcome.”
Use **مِنْ فَضْلِكَ** (min faDlika) to say “please.” It is addressed to one male.

practice.explain: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ means “good morning.” مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ means “good evening.”
شُكْرًا is the Arabic phrase for “thank you.”
مَرْحَبًا means “hello” and is pronounced marhaban.

practice.prompt: Match each Arabic phrase to its English meaning.
practice.explain: عَفْوًا means “you're welcome,” مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ means “goodbye,” and مِنْ فَضْلِكَ means “please” when speaking to one male.

quiz.prompt: Someone says السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. Which reply means “and upon you peace”?
quiz.explain: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ is the reply meaning “and upon you peace.”

quiz.prompt: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ is used to say “good morning.”
quiz.explain: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ means “good evening.” صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ means “good morning.”

quiz.prompt: Write the Latin pronunciation of the Arabic phrase for “thank you.”
quiz.explain: شُكْرًا means “thank you” and is pronounced shukran.

quiz.prompt: Match each phrase to its meaning.
quiz.explain: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ is “good morning,” مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ is “good evening,” and شُكْرًا is “thank you.”

quiz.prompt: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ means “please” when speaking to one male.
quiz.explain: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ is the phrase for “please” addressed to one male.

quiz.prompt: Which phrase is a way to say goodbye?
Write the Latin pronunciation of the reply meaning “and upon you peace.”
quiz.explain: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ is pronounced wa 'alaykumu s-salaam.
